notes: Cross-verified against three CyberPower-hosted sources that all agree: the official product page (cyberpowersystems.com/product/pdu/switched-pdu/pdu41004/), the official PDU41004 datasheet PDF, and the "Power Distribution Units 1U/2U/0U Switched/Metered/Monitored Series" user manual (PDU41004 appears in the 1U-15A IEC-type spec table alongside PDU81004/PDU71004/PDU31004, and its rear/front panel diagram was used to enumerate ports). No Ethernet/RJ45 link speed (e.g. 10/100) is published in any of these documents, so grade was omitted on the Ethernet, Envirosensor/Daisy-Chain-In, Daisy-Chain-Out, and Serial RJ45 ports per the grading rule. The ground stud is a chassis-grounding point, not a signal/data connector — included for completeness but approximated to the closest allowed connector id ("banana"). The serial "port" is physically RJ45 on the unit; DB9 is only present on the included breakout cable, not on the chassis.

ports.name: AC Inlet
ports.note: IEC-320 C14 inlet; 100-240 VAC, 50/60Hz, single phase, 15A max (12A derated), via a captive 10 ft (3.0 m) power cord.

ports.name: AC Output 1
ports.note: IEC-320 C13 switched/controllable outlet, 100-240 VAC. 8 outlets total, all front-mounted in a single bank.

ports.name: Ethernet Port
ports.note: RJ45 network management port for CyberPower PowerPanel Business Edition, web UI, SNMP, Telnet/SSH. No link-speed spec published, so grade is omitted.

ports.name: Envirosensor/Daisy Chain (In) Port
ports.note: RJ45 modular port for the optional CyberPower environmental sensor or for daisy-chaining from a previous PDU; not a data-networking uplink, so no bandwidth grade set.

ports.name: Daisy Chain (Out) Port
ports.note: RJ45 modular port for chaining to the next PDU in a cascade; no bandwidth grade set.

ports.name: Serial Port
ports.note: RJ45 modular serial console port for local SSH/Telnet-style config; ships with an included RJ45-to-DB9 adapter cable — the DB9 connector lives on that cable, not on the unit itself.

ports.name: USB Port
ports.note: Used only to upgrade firmware via a USB flash drive; not a host/data link, so no USB-speed grade set.

ports.name: Ground Stud
ports.note: Rear-panel chassis grounding stud (threaded stud, not a true banana jack) — closest connector id available in the allowed list.
